0|b5b0977f4aa28ef2166894b05f37d8f8028a76ce|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: x86/mmu: Properly account NX huge page workaround for nonpaging MMUs
Account and track NX huge pages for nonpaging MMUs so that a future
enhancement to precisely check if a shadow page can't be replaced by a NX
huge page doesn't get false positives.  Without correct tracking
get stuck in a loop if an instruction is fetching and writing data on the
same huge page
column2: e.g. KVM installs a small executable page on the fetch

column1: fault
column2: replaces it with an NX huge page on the write fault

column1: again on the fetch.
Alternatively
column3: KVM would simply not enforce the

column1: workaround for nonpaging MMUs.  The guest has no page tables to abuse
and KVM is guaranteed to switch to a different MMU on CR0.PG being
toggled so there's no security or performance concerns.  However
make_spte() to play nice now and in the future is unnecessarily complex.
In the current code base
column2: make_spte() can enforce the mitigation if TDP

column1: is enabled or the MMU is indirect
column2: but make_spte() may not always have a

column1: vCPU/MMU to work with
column2: e.g. if KVM were to support in-line huge page

column1: promotion when disabling dirty logging.
Without a vCPU/MMU
column2: KVM could either pass in the correct information

column1: and/or derive it from the shadow page
column2: but the former is ugly and the

column1: latter subtly non-trivial due to the possibility of direct shadow pages
in indirect MMUs.  Given that using shadow paging with an unpaged guest
is far from top priority _and_ has been subjected to the workaround since
its inception
column2: keep it simple and just fix the accounting glitch.
